claims.source_text: Intel’s July investment thesis does not hinge on the Apple deal or Trump’s social media post, topics I’ve written about in the past few issues; rather, it turns on the fact that NVIDIA invested $5B into Intel as well as opted for Intel Xeon 6 as the host CPU in their DGX Rubin NVL8 AI systems. Put another way, it’s the most important GPU company of our day endorsing Intel’s CPU.
claims.meaning: NVIDIA invested $5B in Intel.

claims.source_text: NVIDIA could have gone with any CPU to accompany their Rubin GPU, but they went with Intel Xeon 6 to power the DGX Rubin NVL8, the AI system that will power the data centre for the next two to three years. CEO Lip-Bu Tan recently said Xeon 6 now plays the role of “the orchestration layer and critical control plane for the entire AI stack” and highlighted that the CPU:GPU ratio for inference is beginning to shift from 1-to-8 to 1:1, meaning the ratio of CPUs needed to support the GPU is actually increasing, not decreasing (the prior narrative was that GPUs would ultimately take over the CPU role).

claims.source_text: Under the structure, participating AI clouds procure Nvidia infrastructure and sell Nvidia-powered cloud services to end customers. Nvidia collects its usual product revenue on the hardware plus a percentage of the cloud income earned on that capacity, which the blog post describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. Per Bloomberg , developers receive token credits in exchange for a slice of their future sales, but neither Nvidia nor its partners has disclosed the revenue-split percentages.

claims.source_text: It’s no secret that the credit-support side of this model will help to address a financing gap that Nvidia itself has identified. Even signed, long-term customer commitments have failed to convince lenders to fund large-scale deployments, leaving smaller clouds unable to borrow against the demand they had already generated.
claims.meaning: NVIDIA identifies inability to borrow even against signed long-term customer commitments as the financing gap the credit support addresses.

claims.source_text: In an 8-K filing dated June 12th, Sharon AI disclosed that the agreement runs for six years and covers 72 MW of new Australian data center capacity built to Nvidia's DSX AI factory design, scaling to as many as 40,000 Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs. articles.title: Nvidia's Kyber rack for Rubin Ultra reportedly delayed to 2028, stopgap solution also axed due to customer pushback — Analyst firm SemiAnalysis says PCB midplane problems led to the delay [Updated]

claims.source_text: Update 7/6/2026 4:10pm PT : An Nvidia representative responded with a short statement to Tom's Hardware : "Our roadmap is intact." Nvidia provided no further details in response to our follow-up questions. As such, it is unclear if Nvidia's statement refers to its original roadmap, planned delivery schedules, and hardware, or if those particulars had already been changed and the statement refers to a newly updated roadmap.
claims.meaning: NVIDIA responds that its roadmap is intact; does not specifically clarify unchanged launch schedule.

claims.source_text: Nvidia reportedly won't ship its Kyber NVL144 rack until 2028, a delay of more than 12 months that pushes the cabinet meant for 2027's Rubin Ultra GPUs into the following year, according to a SemiAnalysis thread on X. The holdup is ostensibly being caused by manufacturing challenges with a PCB midplane that connects eight Oberon racks between the NVSwitches, which Nvidia calls the orthogonal backplane. Nvidia is also understood to have killed NVL72x2, a stopgap rack designed to tide customers over, and that no proven alternative is now available to widen Rubin Ultra's scale-up in 2027.
claims.meaning: SemiAnalysis reports Kyber NVL144 delayed from 2027 to 2028 due to PCB midplane manufacturing problems.

claims.source_text: NVL72x2 would have bolted two Oberon racks back-to-back to reach Kyber-class density over copper NVLink, per SemiAnalysis , which said Nvidia abandoned the stopgap after its largest customers balked at running two linked cabinets as a single unit. NVL576, a separate configuration tying eight racks together through co-packaged optics, is likely to slip too or ship in low volume until that optical technology matures.
claims.meaning: NVL72x2 stopgap cancelled after hyperscaler objections to operations and form factor.

claims.source_text: These cancellations leave Nvidia with "no proven solution to expand the scale-up world size for Rubin Ultra," meaning the largest single Rubin Ultra domain in 2027 could match, but not exceed, what Oberon already delivers.
claims.meaning: No proven solution remains to expand Rubin Ultra scale-up in 2027 beyond Oberon.

claims.source_text: Nvidia dropped the quad-chiplet Rubin Ultra GPU for a dual-chiplet part last week over manufacturing execution concerns, halving the accelerator's per-package compute. articles.title: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) Announces a Profit-Sharing Program For Its Computing Framework Access

claims.source_text: On July 1, Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) disclosed a profit-sharing program developed to give model builders, AI startups, and businesses access to Nvidia's computing framework, without the need for these entities to fund hardware buildouts. Under this arrangement, NVIDIA, in addition to product revenue, will receive a share of cloud revenue based on the capacity it supports, as AI cloud providers deliver NVIDIA-powered solutions to their end users.
claims.meaning: NVIDIA launches revenue-sharing access model, receiving cloud usage revenue in addition to hardware sales.

articles.excluded_reason: General demand narration and competition background without a dated/quantified independent development.

original.span: Nvidia has allegedly told the company that the products are on hold because of the price of 3GB GDDR7 memory chips
also: these chips cost twice or thrice as much as their 2GB variants
original.note: Directly moves v19 (RTX 50 SUPER launch by 2027-01-31): the cards exist but are held for memory cost.

original.span: the crunch will last until 2030
also: for the memory shortage
original.note: Supplier says 2027 is the worst year of the memory shortage and it lasts to 2030: memory is the largest cost in NVIDIA's gross margin.

original.span: memory accounting for 25% of the BOM, as costs have soared by nearly 500%
original.note: A figure on NVIDIA's AI-system cost structure; colour for gross margin.

original.span: sees the server CPU total addressable market reaching $170 billion by 2030
original.note: A 2030 TAM estimate; colour for FY2027 stand-alone CPU revenue.

original.span: has agreed to spend as much as $105 billion to support a massive new data center campus in Ohio
also: defined portions of lease and power payments
original.note: The filed obligation: up to $105bn of support for lease and power payments of the OpenAI Ohio campus. Settles v31's direction.

original.span: secure up to roughly 8 gigawatts of computing capacity from the Pike County complex, with the first 800 megawatts expected to come online by 2028
original.note: The customer's commitment and its timetable (800 MW by 2028): the scale behind the guarantee.

original.span: Nvidia has agreed to invest $1.5 billion in SB Energy Corp.
original.note: The SB Energy investment v52 asks about, now agreed.

original.span: very few shipments against licenses for H200s and equivalents have taken place

original.note: An official says H200 shipments to China have started but are very small: moves the H200 permission theses and the China share of FY2027 revenue.

original.span: assessed companies that want the H200 chips on a case-by-case basis
also: There are cases where we deny the license applications we receive
original.note: The US licensing process (case by case, some denials); colour for the H200 theme (the US side has no thesis of its own).

original.span: it expects hyperscaler spending to top $1 trillion in 2027 after reaching a projected $650 billion in 2026
original.who: NVIDIA management (last quarterly call), as reported by the author
original.note: Management's own hyperscaler-capex figures for 2026 and 2027: the demand input for FY2027 revenue and the aggregate-capex theses (another population of the same aggregate is evidence to them).

original.note: Consensus growth rates for this year and next; colour for v2.

original.who: Broadcom (most recent quarter, ended May 3), as reported by the author
original.note: The custom-silicon competitor's AI revenue growth; colour for data center revenue (share of hyperscaler spend).

original.span: the company won a $20 billion deal with OpenAI and also has inked a deal with Amazon Web Services
original.note: A competitor's $20bn inference deal with NVIDIA's largest customer; colour for data center revenue.

original.span: in talks to support as much as $600 billion of OpenAI
also: $250 billion tied to OpenAI’s planned Ohio data center and another $350 billion supporting GPU purchases
original.note: The reported $600bn package: $250bn for the Ohio lease (v31) and $350bn for GPU purchases (v32).

also: backlog of customer orders rose to over half a trillion dollars
original.who: Alphabet (Q2 2026), as reported by the author
original.note: A hyperscaler customer's cloud growth and backlog; colour for data center demand.

also: has officially begun shipping its powerful H200 artificial intelligence chips to China

original.note: H200 shipments to China have begun, in minimal volume: the H200 permission theses and the China share of FY2027 revenue.

original.note: About ten Chinese firms (ZTE unit, Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance) cleared on the US side; colour for the named-company permission theses.

also: ship more B300 GPUs in place of its R200 models

also: are among the latest entities to receive U.S. approval to purchase
original.who: Reuters, from documents and two sources
original.note: Two more Chinese firms licensed by the US for H200: the named-company permission theses widen; China revenue remains the question.

original.span: some Chinese cloud firms have recently told partners and clients they may soon be able to obtain H200 chips
original.note: A sign of progress in China's import reviews, the side v3 asks about.

original.span: released a letter Friday urging policymakers to avoid "premature restrictions" on open-weight artificial intelligence models
also: A group of 25 tech companies released a letter urging policymakers
original.who: NVIDIA, Microsoft, Meta, Palantir and 21 other companies (the letter)
original.note: The industry's step in the open-weight policy process; on 07-24 no thesis on a Chinese-model ban existed yet (v27 opens later from this matter): cold start.

original.span: the Trump administration would look into whether Chinese companies were stealing American intellectual property
original.who: Scott Bessent, U.S. Treasury Secretary, on CNBC
original.note: An official's stated next step (and the sanction power claimed); no thesis yet.

original.span: China's Moonshot AI developed its Kimi K3 model by distilling Anthropic's technology
original.note: The administration's finding that frames the restriction debate; no thesis yet.

original.span: were essential to ensuring that AI is adopted safely and securely across the economy
also: we need open weight for security, we need open weight for safety

original.note: NVIDIA's CEO lobbying the Senate against open-weight curbs: colour for the Chinese-model ban theses.

original.span: the Commerce Department puts the finishing touches on a framework for reviewing the safety of cutting-edge AI models
also: Huang also met with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick
original.who: A person familiar with the matter / Axios, via Bloomberg
original.note: A policy step in preparation (the review framework; v41 opens later from it) and the Lutnick meeting; closest theses are the ban questions.

original.span: I’m not sure this is a genie we can put back in the bottle
original.note: A named policymaker's stance on whether open models can be restricted: moves the ban theses' odds.
